note: Archetypes are data. Adding one is a catalogue edit, not a code change; if a new kind of place needs new code, the placement engine is underspecified and that is the bug to fix. Thresholds are percentile-relative against each world's own distribution, with an absolute floor where 'the best available' should still not qualify on a world that has none of the thing. Spacing is in cell multiples of a fixed reference raster, never the raster in hand, so it is a physical distance that scales with the world and does not change when the same world is sampled more finely.

archetypes.name: Karst cave system
archetypes.reason: Rainwater cut the limestone under a broken slope.

archetypes.name: Sea cave
archetypes.reason: Surf hollowed the headland where no watch can see the entrance.

archetypes.name: Lava tube
archetypes.reason: A drained lava channel runs empty under the flow field.

archetypes.name: Crystal cavern
archetypes.reason: Mineral-rich rock left a hollow lined with grown crystal.

archetypes.name: Sinkhole
archetypes.reason: The roof of a water-cut void gave way and left an open shaft.

archetypes.name: Rift chasm
archetypes.reason: Ground torn along a shearing plate margin and never closed.

archetypes.name: Natural arch
archetypes.reason: Dry wind cut through the weaker band and left the span standing.

archetypes.name: Tar pit
archetypes.reason: Bitumen works up through the basin fill and holds whatever walks in.

archetypes.name: Geyser basin
archetypes.reason: Hot rock near the surface drives the water back out.

archetypes.name: Glacier cave
archetypes.reason: Meltwater bored a passage under the ice and left it open.

archetypes.name: Meteor crater
archetypes.reason: Something came down here and the ring it made never filled in.

archetypes.name: Iron mine
archetypes.reason: Ore in the ridge and a road already running to it.

archetypes.name: Silver mine
archetypes.reason: A rich seam worked from above until the good rock ran out.

archetypes.name: Gem mine
archetypes.reason: Stone worth more than iron, high enough that carrying it out was the hard part.

archetypes.name: Salt mine
archetypes.reason: Rock salt near enough the surface to cut, and salt is worth a road.

archetypes.name: Quarry
archetypes.reason: Workable stone within a cart's haul of somewhere that wanted walls.

archetypes.name: Salt pans
archetypes.reason: Flat brine ground that dries faster than it fills.

archetypes.name: Charcoal burner's camp
archetypes.reason: Standing timber far enough out that nobody minds the smoke.

archetypes.name: Lime kiln
archetypes.reason: Limestone and a road; mortar is made where the stone is.

archetypes.name: Peat cuttings
archetypes.reason: Cut peat dries into the only fuel this ground offers.

archetypes.name: Whaling station
archetypes.reason: Deep water close in and a beach flat enough to haul onto.

archetypes.name: Logging camp
archetypes.reason: Good timber beside water that will float it out.

archetypes.name: Smelter ruin
archetypes.reason: Ore was cooked here; the spoil outlasted everything that used it.

archetypes.name: Border fort
archetypes.reason: A road crossing a border, on the only ground that sees both ways.

archetypes.name: Watchtower
archetypes.reason: High ground that can see the road and be seen from the next tower.

archetypes.name: Hillfort
archetypes.reason: Banks and ditches on a hill, older than anyone still holding the valley.

archetypes.name: Toll station
archetypes.reason: Where the road meets the water, somebody charges for the crossing.

archetypes.name: Linear dyke
archetypes.reason: Somebody dug a line across the open ground and meant it to mean something.

archetypes.name: Refuge broch
archetypes.reason: A drystone tower to climb into when raiders come up the coast.

archetypes.name: Barrow
archetypes.reason: Dry rising ground in sight of where the dead had lived.
archetypes.note: Scatters on its own and is also the member of a barrow ring; both are true of barrows.

archetypes.name: Barrow field
archetypes.reason: Generations buried on the same ridge above the same dead town.

archetypes.name: Mausoleum
archetypes.reason: Cut stone raised for one family who expected to be remembered.

archetypes.name: Cairn field
archetypes.reason: Stones piled by everyone who passed, for reasons nobody agrees on.

archetypes.name: Excarnation tower
archetypes.reason: High dry stone where the dead are given to the birds.

archetypes.name: Ship burial
archetypes.reason: A hull dragged above the tideline and buried with its owner in it.

archetypes.name: Plague pit
archetypes.reason: Dug in a hurry, downwind, and never marked.

archetypes.name: Necropolis
names: the city of the dead at {near}
archetypes.reason: A city that buried more people than it ever housed.

archetypes.name: Cliff coffins
archetypes.reason: Coffins pegged into a rock face nobody can reach without rope.

archetypes.name: Wayside shrine
archetypes.reason: Set where travellers wanted something to thank before going on.

archetypes.name: Monastery
archetypes.reason: Far enough from the world to be quiet, near enough water to live.

archetypes.name: Hermitage
archetypes.reason: Somewhere hard enough to reach that nobody comes twice.

archetypes.name: Sacred grove
archetypes.reason: Old trees nobody will cut, for a reason the local story has kept.

archetypes.name: Standing stones
archetypes.reason: Raised stones on open ground, aligned on something worth aligning on.

archetypes.name: Oracle cave
archetypes.reason: A cleft that answers, or did once, and people still come to ask.

archetypes.name: Holy well
archetypes.reason: Water that never fails, which is reason enough to call it holy.

archetypes.name: Mountain sanctuary
archetypes.reason: Built where the climb is the pilgrimage.

archetypes.name: Drowned temple
archetypes.reason: The water came up and the columns are still standing under it.

archetypes.name: Colossus
archetypes.reason: Carved big enough to be seen from the road, by someone who wanted that.

archetypes.name: Reliquary chapel
archetypes.reason: Built over something small that is worth the detour.

archetypes.name: Crossroads
archetypes.reason: Two roads meeting, which is never only a place to turn.

archetypes.name: Bridge
archetypes.reason: The narrowest crossing on the reach, so the road bends to it.

archetypes.name: Ford
archetypes.reason: Shallow gravel where a laden cart can get across without a bridge.

archetypes.name: Pass hospice
archetypes.reason: The last roof before the pass, kept by whoever is paid to keep it.

archetypes.name: Ferry crossing
archetypes.reason: Too deep to ford and not worth a bridge, so somebody keeps a boat.

archetypes.name: Hedge inn
archetypes.reason: A day's walk from anywhere, which is exactly why it is here.

archetypes.name: Gibbet
archetypes.reason: Put where the road can see it, which is the whole point of it.

archetypes.name: Caravanserai
archetypes.reason: Water in dry country, walled, because water in dry country needs walls.

archetypes.name: Ley nexus
archetypes.reason: Where the lines cross, the ground remembers it.

archetypes.name: Wizard's tower
archetypes.reason: Strong ground, far from anyone who would ask what the noise was.

archetypes.name: Wild-magic scar
archetypes.reason: Something went wrong here and the ground has not agreed to forget.

archetypes.name: Binding site
archetypes.reason: Built to hold one thing, and nothing else was built anywhere near it.

archetypes.name: Portal arch
archetypes.reason: A standing frame with nothing on the other side of it, most days.

archetypes.name: Mage academy ruin
archetypes.reason: They taught something here until it taught them back.

archetypes.name: Summoning circle
archetypes.reason: Cut into the turf by someone who did not want to be interrupted.

archetypes.name: Petrified army
archetypes.reason: Ranks of figures in stone, still facing the way they were told to.

archetypes.name: Dragon lair
archetypes.reason: High, defensible, and within a day's flight of something worth taking.

archetypes.name: Giant's hall
archetypes.reason: Built at a scale nobody local could have raised.

archetypes.name: Spider wood
archetypes.reason: Dense wet timber nobody has thinned in a long time.

archetypes.name: Beast den
archetypes.reason: Sheltered ground with prey below and nobody hunting it.

archetypes.name: Wyvern eyrie
archetypes.reason: A ledge nothing without wings can reach.

archetypes.name: Drowned village
archetypes.reason: The water came up faster than the roofs came down.

archetypes.name: Wreck field
archetypes.reason: Shoal water on a course ships kept taking anyway.

archetypes.name: Surf-line ruin
archetypes.reason: Built on a shore that has since moved inland.

archetypes.name: Crannog
archetypes.reason: An island built by hand because an island is easier to hold.

archetypes.name: Crater of the fallen star
archetypes.reason: Something fell out of the sky and the world is still shaped around it.

archetypes.name: Titan skeleton
archetypes.reason: Ribs standing out of the ground like a roofless hall.

archetypes.name: The great stump
archetypes.reason: A cut surface wide enough to build a village on, and someone did.

archetypes.name: The Scar
archetypes.reason: The ground opened along the whole plate margin and stayed open.

archetypes.name: The standing maelstrom
archetypes.reason: Water turning in one place for longer than anyone has records for.

archetypes.name: Observatory
archetypes.reason: Clear dry air and height, because the moons are worth watching properly.

archetypes.name: Library ruin
archetypes.reason: What burned was the roof; what is under it may not have burned.

archetypes.name: Lighthouse
archetypes.reason: A headland that has taken enough ships to be worth a fire on.

archetypes.name: Quarantine isle
archetypes.reason: Close enough to supply, far enough that nothing walks back.

archetypes.name: Arena ruin
archetypes.reason: A bowl of seats around a floor that has soaked up a great deal.

archetypes.name: Aqueduct span
archetypes.reason: Carried water to somewhere that no longer needs any.

archetypes.name: Fairy ring
archetypes.reason: A ring in the grass that the locals walk around rather than through.

archetypes.name: Witch's cottage
archetypes.reason: Out past the last field, which is where you go when you want to be found on purpose.

archetypes.name: Bandit camp
archetypes.reason: Cover within a dash of the road and a long ride from the nearest garrison.

archetypes.name: Hunting lodge
archetypes.reason: Good hunting and a roof for whoever owns the right to it.

archetypes.name: Regrown battlefield
archetypes.reason: Flat open ground beside a road, which is where armies agree to meet.

archetypes.name: Waystone
archetypes.reason: Counted out along the road so a traveller knows how much is left.

archetypes.name: Boundary stone
archetypes.reason: Cut where one claim ends, by people who expected to be argued with.

archetypes.name: Beacon tower
archetypes.reason: Sited so the next beacon can see it, and lit when it must not be alone.

archetypes.name: Pilgrim station
names: the {ordinal} station on the road to {near}
archetypes.reason: A day's walk apart on the approach, for people who arrive on foot.

archetypes.name: Siege camp
archetypes.reason: Dug in sight of the walls by whoever was waiting them out.

archetypes.name: Miners' cottages
archetypes.reason: Built where the shift ended, and emptied when it stopped.

archetypes.name: Hermit's cell
archetypes.reason: Far enough from the house to be alone, near enough to be fed.

succession.note: What moves into a place after the builders leave, applied only to sites already in an abandoned-like state and only once at least one age has passed. This is where dungeons come from: no archetype is called a dungeon, and none needs to be.

extractive.note: Worked out, propped up, and then taken by whatever found the entrance.

fortification.note: Walls outlive garrisons, and walls are worth having.

sacred.note: A roof and an altar attract a different congregation.

subterranean.note: Nothing has to move in; something usually does.

arcane.note: Whatever was being worked on is still there.

curiosity.note: Somebody always finds a use for a standing roof.

drowned.note: What lives there now got there by water.

wayside.note: An empty house on a road does not stay empty.

chains.name: Waystone line
chains.reason: A road nobody has counted out is a road nobody has walked often.

chains.name: March stones
chains.reason: A border is only a line because somebody put stones along it.

chains.name: Beacon line
chains.reason: Each one sited so the next can see it; a beacon that stands alone is only a tower.

chains.name: Pilgrim stations
chains.reason: Spaced along the last approach, because the arrival is the point and the walk is the rest of it.

clusters.name: Siege works
clusters.reason: Somebody was outside these walls long enough to build.

clusters.name: Mine village
clusters.reason: Nobody walks far to a shift; the village is always within sight of the head.

clusters.name: Barrow ring
clusters.reason: The big tombs drew the smaller ones around them for generations.

clusters.name: Hermit cells
clusters.reason: A house of people who wanted quiet attracts people who wanted more of it.
